articles.headline: Scientists Just Found a Shortcut: Use Existing Drugs to Slow Aging
articles.body: Northeastern researchers discovered that aging-related genes form a network linked to the hallmarks of aging. The breakthrough means scientists can now search through existing approved drugs to find ones that might reverse or slow aging. This isn't about inventing new treatments from scratch—it's about finding hidden superpowers in medications already on pharmacy shelves. The findings could dramatically accelerate the timeline for bringing longevity therapies to market. No more waiting decades for new drug development.
articles.takeaway: Existing drugs may hold anti-aging potential. Talk to your doctor about which ones might apply to your specific aging markers.

articles.topic: sleep quality next day cognitive performance
articles.headline: One Bad Night Tanked Your Brain Today. Here's Why It Matters
articles.body: New research shows that sleep quality—not just quantity—predicts how sharp you'll be the next day. Older adults who experienced poor sleep quality performed worse on cognitive tests the following morning, even if they'd slept long enough. The issue isn't so much about logging eight hours; it's about spending those hours in deep, uninterrupted rest. Night wakings are the real culprit. This finding changes everything about how we should approach sleep: consistency and depth matter more than pure duration for maintaining mental edge.
articles.takeaway: Focus on sleep quality, not just hours. Minimize night wakings and prioritize unbroken rest for better next-day cognition.

articles.headline: Reading for Pleasure Might Be Your Brain's Best Defense
articles.body: Cambridge researchers analyzed decades of studies and found reading for pleasure is linked to better cognitive performance, structural brain changes, lower stress, and significantly reduced dementia risk in later life. Adults who read regularly showed a 35 percent lower risk of dementia. Even more impressive: reading can offset cognitive decline that typically comes with less formal education. The benefits start early—childhood reading predicts better memory and attention in adulthood. Brain scans show that reading actually changes brain structure, strengthening regions critical for language and memory.
articles.takeaway: Make reading a non-negotiable part of your day. Even 20 minutes of literary fiction activates stress-reducing brain networks.

articles.topic: wearable sensors clinical grade health monitoring
articles.headline: Your Smartwatch Just Became a Legit Medical Device
articles.body: Wearable sensors have crossed a major threshold. A comprehensive review shows they're now achieving clinical-grade accuracy for rehabilitation monitoring, disease risk assessment, and activity tracking. Smartwatches can detect Parkinson's tremors with 83 percent accuracy and predict fall risk with 86 percent precision. The tech is accurate enough that hospitals are starting to integrate wearable data into actual patient records. This isn't fitness tracking anymore—it's real-time health surveillance that your doctor can actually trust and act on. The barrier wasn't the technology; it was proving the data was reliable.
articles.takeaway: Your wearable data now has clinical value. Share it with your healthcare provider if they're set up to use it.

workout.title: Walk-Run Pyramid: Building the Base
workout.tip: Keep your shoulders relaxed and land with a midfoot strike. If you feel breathless during the running intervals, slow down by 0.5 mph—comfort over speed at this stage.
workout.warmup: 2 min @ 2.5 mph / 0% incline (easy walk) + 1 min @ 3.0 mph / 0% incline (brisk walk)

exercises.name: Walk-Run Interval Pyramid
exercises.notes: Execute the following sequence: 1 min walk @ 3.2 mph / 0% + 1 min run @ 5.0 mph / 0% → 1 min walk @ 3.2 mph / 0% + 2 min run @ 5.0 mph / 0% → 1 min walk @ 3.2 mph / 0% + 3 min run @ 5.0 mph / 0% → 1 min walk @ 3.2 mph / 0% + 2 min run @ 5.0 mph / 0% → 1 min walk @ 3.2 mph / 0% + 1 min run @ 5.0 mph / 0%. Focus on steady breathing and relaxed arm swing throughout all transitions.

workout.cooldown: 2 min @ 3.0 mph / 0% incline (easy walk). Post-run: hamstring stretch 30 sec each leg, quad stretch 30 sec each leg, calf stretch 20 sec each leg.
workout.description: A structured walk-run progression designed for complete beginners or runners returning from a long break. This session uses a pyramid format to build confidence and aerobic capacity without overload, perfect for establishing a sustainable treadmill routine before progressing to continuous running.

meal.title: Chicken, Rice & Broccoli Meal-Prep Bowl
meal.description: The meal-prep classic: seasoned chicken breast, rice and broccoli with a splash of soy. Make 4 at once.
meal.instructions: 1. Season the chicken and cook in the oil 6–7 minutes per side (or bake 20 minutes at 400°F); slice. 2. Steam the broccoli 4 minutes. 3. Divide the rice, chicken and broccoli into containers and drizzle with soy sauce. Keeps 4 days in the fridge.
